To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) LDA was used to determine if T lymphocytes specific for periodontal bacteria are present in the peripheral blood; (ii) the frequency of periodontal-bacteria-specific T lymphocytes was not significantly different between patients with gingivitis or periodontitis and controls; and (iii) the frequency of tetanus toxoid-specific T lymphocytes did not differ significantly between the three groups.

LDA was used to determine if periodontopathic-bacterium-specific T cells were present in the peripheral blood, and that they were found in all groups, although the frequencies were not significantly different.
the frequencies of peripheral blood T cells reactive to the two test antigens were similar in the three groups, and that the kinetics of the response to the test antigens were generally'single-hit'.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple, rapid and reproducible method for the detection of periodontopathic bacteria-specific T cells.

the development of a method for detecting the presence and frequency in peripheral blood of T lymphocytes which have been activated by periodontopathic bacteria and which may therefore play a role in the pathogenesis of periodontal disease.
a better understanding of the role that the immune response plays in the pathogenesis of periodontal disease.

the frequency of periodontopathogen-specific T cells in patients with periodontitis is similar to that in non-periodontitis patients.

the results of the current study indicate that the peripheral blood T lymphocyte response to B. gingivatis and A. viscosum is similar in healthy and periodontally diseased subjects.
we have shown the presence of specific T cells to B. gingivialis and A. viscosous in the peripheral blood.
the presence of periodontopathic bacterial-specific T cells in peripheral blood is not associated with periodontitis.

the frequency of PTL-p specific for periodontal pathogens is similar in patients with periodontitis compared to those without.
